subject: general
question: If ₹12,000 is deposited in a simple interest account that yields 10% annually, what will be the interest earned after two and a half years?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Effective rate** of interest = Rate × Time

Effective rate = 10% × 2.5 = 25%

Interest = 25% of **Principal** = 25% of ₹12,000

Interest = 12,000 ÷ 4 = 3,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Principal** (P) = ₹12,000

**Rate** (R) = 10% per annum

**Time** (T) = 2.5 years

**Formula Used:**

**Simple Interest** (SI) = (P × R × T) / 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b692818a6756071ca614f34563209c898f31b845195bd15ddd6a5a1a32aec5e1.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = (12000 × 10 × 2.5) / 100

⇒ SI = 120 × 10 × 2.5

⇒ SI = 1200 × 2.5

⇒ SI = 3000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Amount Calculation

The **Total Amount** (A) is the sum of the principal and the interest earned: A = P + SI. In this case, A = 12,000 + 3,000 = ₹15,000.

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

In **Simple Interest**, the principal remains constant for the entire duration. In **Compound Interest**, the interest from previous periods is added to the principal for the next calculation.

Time Conversion

Always ensure **Time** (T) is in years when the **Rate** (R) is per annum. For example, 6 months should be used as 0.5 years in the formula.
